performance_claim_scope: Clean W7900 post-LCP-4A chain_peer_wave32 512/4K floor recheck; exact/peer/llama.cpp kernel-family profiles remain diagnostic crosswalks.
purpose: Reprofile the clean production-exact GGUF route after LCP-4A removed normal Conv private storage, then compare it with the clean quality-admitted peer-GDN route, llama.cpp HIP, and the retained PARO schedule control. This identifies the shipped pp512 deficit without selecting from stale pre-LCP-4A family totals.

protocol.hipengine_profile: For each route, create one cached-only max-512 resident session, run initialization prefill, reset, run the identical warm prefill five seconds before the target, reset, and collect only the final synchronized pp512 prefill in a bounded rocprofv3 collection window.
protocol.peer_speed_gate: One clean max-4K resident session; per shape one discarded warmup and three measured prefill/decode runs; graph capture excluded from decode throughput; cached builds required.
protocol.llamacpp_profile: Retained same-W7900 llama-bench pp512 measured pass isolated as 2,259 dispatches after its warmup pass.
protocol.comparability_note: hipEngine exact and peer rows use the same commit, model, prompt, device, and profile protocol. llama.cpp uses the same Q4_K_M file but F16 KV and differently fused families. PARO is a different W4 model/quant and older software revision, so it is a schedule control only. Internal routing differences can change selected-MoE row counts; family crosswalks are measured execution totals, not primitive A/Bs.

commands.hipengine_profile_template: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 HIPENGINE_BACKEND=hip_gfx1100 HIPENGINE_HIP_ARCH=gfx1100 HIPENGINE_GGUF_GDN_PREFILL_MODE=<chain_lds32_direct|chain_peer_wave32> HIPENGINE_COMPILER_VERSION_FILE=/tmp/hipengine-hipcc-version-gpf9c.txt HIPENGINE_PROFILE_TARGET_START_SECONDS=120 HIPENGINE_PROFILE_WARMUP_LEAD_SECONDS=5 PYTHONPATH=/home/lhl/hipEngine-main rocprofv3 --kernel-trace --output-format csv --collection-period 119:10:1 --output-directory <tmp> --output-file <route> --log-level error -- python3 /tmp/profile_gpf9c_collection_window.py
commands.peer_speed_gate: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 HIPENGINE_BACKEND=hip_gfx1100 HIPENGINE_HIP_ARCH=gfx1100 HIPENGINE_GGUF_GDN_PREFILL_MODE=chain_peer_wave32 HIPENGINE_COMPILER_VERSION_FILE=/tmp/hipengine-hipcc-version-gpf9c.txt PYTHONPATH=. python3 scripts/qwen35_readme_sweep.py --engine gguf --model /models/gguf/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf --quant gguf_q4_k_m --backend hip_gfx1100 --workloads 512/128 4K/128 --warmup-runs 1 --measured-runs 3 --warmup-decode-tokens 1 --force-bulk-prefill --bulk-prefill-attention-mode bulk --use-wmma-prefill --use-gemv-decode --graph-replay-decode --graph-steps-per-replay 1 --compiler-version-file /tmp/hipengine-hipcc-version-gpf9c.txt --require-cached-build --json /tmp/gpf9c-post-lcp4a-clean-c85c2880.json

production_exact.geometry: 32-thread workgroup, 4,096 total grid threads; one thread owns one value column and evaluates all 128 state rows in scalar order; 16,384 bytes LDS/workgroup

peer_wave32.geometry: 128-thread workgroup, 131,072 total grid threads; one wave32 owns one value column, keeps four state rows/lane in VGPRs, and uses the llama.cpp XOR reduction tree; zero LDS

llamacpp_hip.geometry: One wave32 owns one value column and keeps four state rows/lane resident across the serial token loop

paro_schedule_control.note: Different model, quant, protocol, and software revision; useful only to confirm that state-row parallel recurrence is the known fast hipEngine schedule.

delta_summary.interpretation: The production GDN excess is larger than the whole kernel/span deficit because selected Q4/Q5 and remaining glue are faster than llama.cpp. The peer route removes the first-order GDN excess; its summed GPU work is within 0.507 ms of llama.cpp and its remaining trace-span difference is 3.071 ms.

post_lcp4a_peer_speed_gate.decision: Keep chain_peer_wave32 explicit-only. LCP-4A materially narrows the 512 miss, but the prospectively frozen rule requires both 512 and 4K to meet the llama.cpp floors; 512 remains 1.104% below.

conclusion: The shipped pp512 gap is the scalar-order exact GDN recurrence, not GGUF broadly. Production exact spends 199.030 ms in the GDN chain versus 16.522 ms in llama.cpp; that +182.508 ms excess exceeds the whole +180.317 ms trace-span gap. After substituting the already quality-admitted peer schedule, hipEngine and llama.cpp perform essentially equal GPU work (203.808 vs 203.301 ms), with only 3.071 ms of trace-span residual. Conv is now 1.977 ms and closed as a first-order target. The clean peer route still misses the frozen 512 non-profiled floor by 1.104%, so production remains chain_lds32_direct.
next: Do not reopen dense-Q8, selected-MoE, Conv, full-attention, or generic launch-count experiments to explain the shipped gap. Any parity continuation should preserve the admitted peer GDN schedule and target its final approximately 3 ms queue/span residual or produce genuinely new exact-parallel GDN evidence; re-run the full semantic/decode gate before any future peer-route promotion.
